name: Numbers Protocol
rootCause: According to the intelligence of the SlowMist security team, the Numbers Protocol (NUM) token project on the ETH chain was attacked, and the attacker made a profit of about $13,836. The main reason for this attack is that the NUM token does not have a permit function and has a callback function, so a fake signature can be passed in to deceive the cross-chain bridge and cause the user's assets to be transferred out unexpectedly.

descriptions.text: According to the intelligence of the SlowMist security team, the Numbers Protocol (NUM) token project on the ETH chain was attacked, and the attacker made a profit of about $13,836. The main reason for this attack is that the NUM token does not have a permit function and has a callback function, so a fake signature can be passed in to deceive the cross-chain bridge and cause the user's assets to be transferred out unexpectedly.

On 23 November 2022, the Numbers Protocol NUM token suffered a targeted exploit due to a logic flaw when interacting with the Multichain bridge. The attacker emptied over 557,754 NUM (~$13,800) from a user’s account by abusing a missing permit function, converting the tokens to USDC and WETH on Ethereum. The NUM ERC-20 token did not implement the permit (EIP-2612) function expected by the Multichain bridge. The Multichain router attempted to use permit for in-transaction token approval but instead triggered the NUM token’s fallback behavior, allowing a fake signature to bypass permission checks and transfer tokens from user wallets.
